title: Venn Diagrams
intro: Venn-diagram questions come in two flavours. The logical type asks which diagram best shows the relation between given groups (e.g., Dogs, Animals, Cats). The numerical type gives a diagram with numbers in each region and asks for a count — how many are in exactly one set, in both, in none. Decide first whether groups are fully contained, overlapping, or separate; for counts, work region by region and never double-count the overlap.

items.name: One contains another
items.formula: e.g. all dogs are animals → Dogs inside Animals

items.name: Partial overlap
items.formula: some shared, some not → intersecting circles

topics.name: Representing Sets
topics.details: Pick the diagram that matches real relationships. Use containment when one group is wholly part of another; overlap when groups share some members; separate circles when groups can't share members.

solved.solution: Dogs and Cats are separate circles, both inside Animals.
Mothers inside Women; Doctors overlap both (some doctors are women/mothers).
Pencil and Pen are separate, both inside Stationery.
Three overlapping circles — a person can be any combination.

hints: Men & Women separate; Doctors overlap both.

topics.name: Logical Venn (Items)
topics.details: These name three or four items and ask for the matching figure. The skill is judging real-world containment and overlap. Watch for items that look related but are disjoint (e.g., 'Even numbers, Odd numbers, Numbers' → two separate inside one).

solved.problem: Even numbers, Prime numbers, Numbers — diagram?
solved.solution: Evens and Primes overlap only at 2; both inside Numbers.
Apple inside Fruit; Vegetable separate from both.
Table and Chair separate, both inside Furniture.

hints: Author & Poet may overlap, inside Person.

topics.name: Numerical Venn
topics.details: A diagram gives counts in each region; you compute totals. Use |A∪B| = |A| + |B| − |A∩B| for two sets. 'Only A' means A minus the overlap.

solved.problem: From the same data, how many are in only A?
40 like tea, 30 like coffee, 12 like both. How many like only one?

unsolved.problem: 25 play cricket, 20 hockey, 8 both. Only one game?

topics.name: Region Counting
topics.details: Three-set diagrams have seven regions: three 'only', three 'pair-only', and one 'all three'. Fill from the centre: subtract the all-three count from each pairwise total to get 'pair-only', then subtract everything from each single total to get 'only'.

solved.problem: |A∩B∩C| = 6, |A∩B| = 14. Members in A and B but not C?

shortcuts: Ask "can one thing be in both groups?" — never ⇒ separate circles.
For three sets, fill from the centre outward.
mistakes: Double-counting the intersection in a union.
Treating overlapping groups as separate (or vice versa).
Forgetting the "none/outside" region in a total.
In three-set counts, not subtracting the centre from pair totals.
pyq: SSC Tier 1 asks one logical-Venn item; Tier 2 adds numerical region counting. The union formula and centre-out filling cover every numerical case.
summary: For logical Venn, judge containment/overlap/separation from real meaning. For numerical Venn, use |A∪B| = |A|+|B|−|A∩B|, read "only" as set-minus-overlap, and fill three-set diagrams from the centre so every region is counted exactly once.
